metadata.title: Q1 environment and identity qualification of the V2 target topology

definition.purpose: Decide, before any V2 reliability experiment runs, whether one local environment holds the target topology of the desired-state release: two platform API replicas and two serving runtime replicas, delivered by the controller at the desired revision, with both runtime replicas verifying the pinned model, and with the caller runner completing real requests through the API Service. The result is QUALIFIED or REFUSED.
definition.scope: One release of the support assistant, key local-docker-desktop/support-assistant, delivered by the controller from the remote main, on the docker-desktop provider. One capacity reading before the Application is applied, one reading of the release, and one RP-1 run of the caller runner for each qualification.
definition.revisionReason: Revision 1 records the exact environment identity, which holds the memory figures of the node and of the container engine to the byte. On 2026-10-16 the Q3 characterization q3-1 was refused on that identity: after a start of the Docker Desktop virtual machine, the container engine and the node reported 10,429,972,480 bytes where q1-1 states 10,429,960,192, and a later start reported 10,429,956,096. The two capacity records state the same provider, server version, node, kubelet version, CPU figures, and pods; only the memory figures differ. A memory figure is a reading of one start of the virtual machine. ADR-0021 decides that the environment identity states the facts of the configuration and that memory is a capacity fact, which the capacity gate decides for each reading. This revision records the stable environment identity, revision 2, which holds no memory figure. It changes no acceptance criterion, no target, no bound, and no step of the driver. q1-1 stays a record of revision 1, with its exact identity and its digest.
definition.notResultEvidence: Q1 is a qualification and not a reliability experiment. No qualification is a result of E02, E03, E04, E05, or E06. It injects no fault, and it derives no bound: that is later work. No figure of the caller run is a latency, a throughput, an availability, or a threshold, and no claim cites one.
definition.repetitionRule: One qualification for each identifier. A qualification is never repeated for a cleaner outcome. A refused qualification is kept, and the refusal is not converted into a weaker target: no replica count, request, limit, or bound is changed to obtain QUALIFIED. A later qualification runs only after the environment or a frozen input changes, under a later revision of this record when a frozen input changes, and it takes the next identifier.
definition.selectedEnvironmentRule: When a qualification is QUALIFIED, its record states the stable environment identity and its digest. E02A and E02B execute in an environment of that identity. A run of either states its own stable environment identity, and a run whose identity differs from the qualified one is not a run of the controlled comparison. The identity holds no memory figure, so each run is also held to the capacity gate on its own capacity reading, and a reading that the gate refuses refuses the run. When the local environment is REFUSED, the refusal is retained, and a separate environment decision record precedes any other environment.
limitations: One provider, one node, one Kubernetes version, and one release. Nothing here is portable to another environment.

The tool reads the stored source records. It does not build the capacity, endpoint, model cache, reconciliation, or provenance records again. The driver runs each tool on its collection in the same qualification, and the transcript shows each run.
The capacity reading is taken before the Application is applied, because the gate refuses a cluster that already holds the release. It states requests and limits, not use.

The model cache observation states the V1 multi-replica capacity preflight and the readiness of each pod while it loads. Q1 does not run the V1 preflight and does not sample the start, so those two rules of the observation are not read.

The controller version is the version that the bootstrap procedure pins, and not a version that the cluster reported. The verification of the bootstrap procedure compares the installation with that pin, and Q1 reads the exit status of that verification.
The direct kubectl and Helm commands of the driver name the context docker-desktop and run no target check of their own. The operating procedures that the driver calls each run it.
The caller run is one bounded RP-1 run. Its success count shows that the path answered. It is not a rate.

The stable environment identity holds no memory figure. Two environments of one identity can report other memory. The capacity gate decides for each reading whether the declared limits and the reserve fit the memory that the node allocates, and it does not compare the memory of two readings.
doesNotEstablish: A recovery time, an availability, a service level, a capacity figure, or a threshold.
A runtime start time, a caller gap, or any bound that later work derives.
Behaviour under a fault, under the replacement of a pod, or under a rollout.
Behaviour on another provider, on more than one node, or with another release.
That the telemetry or the infrastructure state is caller truth. The caller record is the caller's own record.
That memory above the declared limits and the reserve has no effect on a later measurement, or why the virtual machine reports other memory figures after each start.

parts.title: Environment and identity qualification
parts.question: Can the selected local environment hold the declared target topology at its exact identities, with the controller reconciled, both runtime replicas on the pinned model, and the caller runner completing real requests through the API Service?
procedure: Prepare the release once, with the phase up of the driver, from the committed tree with a clean working tree and with every material file at its pin: the capacity gate before anything is installed; the API image built at the executing commit; the model cache claim filled from the local seed image by one preparation Helm release that is then removed; the delivery controller installed and verified by its bootstrap procedure; the capacity gate again, which is the reading that Q1 reads; the Application applied; and the two rollouts waited for, with a bound of 900 s each. The phase up writes its start time first. When it then refuses on a working tree that is not clean, delivery paths that differ from the remote main, a changed material file, a cluster that already holds the release or the controller, or a refusal of the target check or of the capacity gate, or fails at a preparation step, it keeps the reason as upRefusal, installs nothing more, and changes nothing to fit.

Start a qualification with the phase qualify of the driver. Read the executing commit, the working tree, the desired revision as the remote main, whether the chart, the desired-state tree, and the controller manifests of the executing commit equal those of that revision, and whether the freeze tool lists a changed material file. Refuse an identifier whose directory exists or that a collector already used. When the phase up refused or failed, or one of these is not at its state, read no cluster state and go to the header.
Resolve the provenance of the target release key at the desired revision. Verify the delivery controller with its bootstrap procedure.
Take 5 reconciliation samples, 10 s apart, and build the reconciliation record with the provenance comparison of the target release key.
Read the Deployments of the release. Take one endpoint reading of the two Services.

Observe the model cache in each runtime pod: the verification log, the mount table, the file identity, one model listing, and one completion through a port-forward to that pod. Build the model cache record.

Run the caller runner once: RP-1 against the API Service for 60 s with a request ceiling of 50, with the provenance release identifier. Wait for the Job, at most 600 s. Collect the caller record, and clean up the runner.
Write the header of the directory, and build the Q1 record with the tool. Keep the record when the tool exits 0 (QUALIFIED) or 5 (REFUSED). The record states the result. The driver states none.

value.definition: This record states the purpose, the procedure, and the acceptance criteria in full. A change to any of them, or to a pinned input, is a new revision of this record.

value.pinnedInputs: Every file in materialScope is pinned by its content digest in pinnedInputs. A record cannot name the commit that adds it, so the pins freeze the files and not a commit.
value.executingRevision: Each qualification runs at a commit that holds this record, with a clean working tree. The collections and the header name that commit. The delivery controller reads the remote main, and the driver reads no cluster state when the chart, the desired-state tree, or the controller manifests of the executing commit differ from it.

value.provider: docker-desktop, selected explicitly. Each operating procedure that the driver calls runs the target check before its own reads and mutations. The direct kubectl and Helm commands of the driver name the context docker-desktop and run no target check
value.nodes: one node, which the capacity record states and on which the runtime pods run
value.recordedPerQualification: The stable environment identity: the provider, the server version, each node with its kubelet version and the CPU and the pods that it allocates, and the CPU count of the container engine, as the capacity record states them, with identityRevision 2, and the SHA-256 of their canonical text. It holds no memory figure
value.selection: A QUALIFIED record selects this environment for E02A and E02B. A REFUSED record is retained, and no weaker target replaces it.
value.capacity: Memory is a capacity fact. The capacity record of each qualification states the memory of the node and of the container engine, and the capacity gate decides whether the declared limits and the reserve fit it: Q1-AC9 requires ACCEPTED. A later run is held to the gate on its own capacity reading

value.runner: tools/reliability_runner/incluster.py in a Job of the release namespace, started by scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh

value.delivery: The Application local-docker-desktop-support-assistant renders the chart at the commit that main names, with the generated values of the support assistant and the hand-written values of the Application.
value.runner: One Job, one ConfigMap, and one network policy for the qualification, in the release namespace, removed by its cleanup.

fault.reason: Q1 injects no fault. It reads the release once while it is at its declared state.

repetitionCount.value: No result-bearing run. One qualification for each identifier, under definition.repetitionRule.

value.statement: The target check of the operating procedures selected the target and refused nothing.
The qualification selects the docker-desktop provider explicitly, the target check refused no provider, and every source record that names a provider names docker-desktop.

The target check found one target, the cluster held no release and no controller before the phase up, the capacity collection names the context docker-desktop, the capacity record holds one node and a readable environment identity, and the runtime pods run on that node.
The working tree was clean when the phase up started and when the qualification started.
The driver names the Q1 freeze record, the record has the content that the checkout holds, and the freeze tool listed no changed material file in the phase up or in the qualification.

The desired revision is one full commit identifier, and the chart, the desired-state tree, and the controller manifests of the executing commit equal those of that revision in the phase up and in the qualification.
The capacity collection, the endpoint collection, the model cache collection, and the reconciliation collection name the executing commit of the qualification.
The provenance record resolves the target release key at the desired revision to one release identifier.
The V2 capacity gate accepted the target release key with 2 API replicas and 2 runtime replicas before the release was applied.
The verification of the delivery controller by its bootstrap procedure exited 0, and the driver states the controller version.

The reconciliation record is complete, holds at least 5 samples, and in each sample the Application is settled at the desired revision, resolves to the provenance release, and has no finding in its revisions, its source, and its labels.

The phase up completed its preparation, and the API Deployment and the runtime Deployment of the release each state 2 replicas, and each reports 2 replicas, 2 Ready, 2 available, and 2 updated at its current generation.
The endpoint record is OBSERVED, and the API Service and the runtime Service each have 2 endpoints, and both are Ready.
The api container of the API Deployment runs the API image digest that the driver built and declared, and the runtime container of the runtime Deployment runs the pinned runtime image.

The copies of the model pin and the runtime image pin have the content that the freeze record pins, the model cache record expects that model and that runtime image for 2 runtime replicas of the target release, and it holds each of its model identity rules.

The runner's reader accepts the caller record with its plan, in the mode in-cluster, for this qualification and the provenance release, the run ended by its own bound, and at least one request has the outcome success.

The capacity reading precedes the qualification, and the endpoint reading, the model cache collection, the start of the caller run, and the first and the last reconciliation samples lie between the start and the end of the qualification.

derivedNumericBounds.reason: Q1 derives no bound. Any bound is derived by later work, after a QUALIFIED Q1. The durations of the driver are bounds of the procedure, not acceptance bounds.

files.run.json: The header that the driver wrote.
files.capacity/: The capacity collection that the record reads, with its record.
files.provenance.json: The provenance of the target release at the desired revision.
files.reconciliation/, reconciliation.record.j: The reconciliation observation and its record.
files.endpoints/: The endpoint collection, with its record.
files.model-cache/: The model cache collection, with its record.
files.plan.json, caller.jsonl: The plan of the caller run and the caller record.
files.caller.refused.jsonl: The caller log that a rule of its reader refused, when one was refused.
files.pins/model-source.v1.json, pins/containe: The two pin files as the qualification read them. The tool holds each to the content that this record pins.
files.record.v1alpha1.json: The Q1 record, which states the result.
files.transcript.txt: What the phases printed, with the absolute path of the host removed.

value.notCommitted: Raw cluster answers that hold addresses or the whole pod list of other namespaces, when a later change decides to redact them, are named in the run page with what was removed.

value: A tracked file changes while the qualification runs.
A person changes a replica count, a request, a limit, or an object of the release while the qualification runs.
The cluster that the target check verifies is not the docker-desktop provider.
abortConditions.note: An abort is stated in the run page, and the qualification is kept with the result that its record states.

value: The phase qualify cleans up the caller runner and reads the objects that carry the label of the qualification.
Keep the collections under .artifacts/ until the run directory is assembled.

After the last qualification, remove the Application, the controller, and the prerequisite layer with the phase down of the driver, and compare the namespaces and the custom resource definitions with those that the phase up read before it installed anything.

intendedEvidenceLevel.note: Runtime: a real cluster, the delivery controller, the real runtime, and the real model on one provider and one node. A qualification is a prerequisite and not a result, and its level does not raise the level of any claim.

materialScope.description: The path of one qualification. The import closure of the nine tools that the driver runs; the driver; the nine procedures that it calls and the bootstrap record of the controller; the file that the caller runner executes in the cluster; the RP-1 profile and the V1 load profile that RP-1 reads; the model source record and the runtime container package, which pin the model and the runtime image; the chart, the desired-state tree with the contract and the environment binding it is rendered from, and the two manifests of the delivery controller, which together decide the release; the Terraform prerequisite layer; the two image build files and the build's ignore file; the whole inferops package that the API image copies; and the dependency lock.

inputChanges.reason: The driver names revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record as the record that it holds the material files to. Its steps are unchanged.
The package exports the names that the module adds. No rule reads it.

The module states the stable environment identity, revision 2, for a record of revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record, and the exact identity for a record of revision 1. It builds each record under the revision its header names. It names revision 2 as its freeze record.
